title: Gangtok
selection: Batch 1. Gangtok already had 8 attraction pages and itineraries but a thin town page. places.name: Gangtok
places.summary: Sikkim's hill capital at 1,650 m: MG Marg, monasteries, Kanchenjunga views and the base for Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La.
places.seoTitle: Gangtok Travel Guide: MG Marg, Permits & Getting Around
places.seoDescription: Plan a Gangtok trip: MG Marg and Lal Market, monasteries, the cable car, taxis and shared jeeps, permits for Nathu La, monsoon landslides and Sikkimese food.

overview.text:
Gangtok, Sikkim's capital, spreads across a ridge at about 1,650 m with views west to Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak. Life centres on MG Marg, the pedestrian promenade, and on Lal Market. Monasteries such as Rumtek and Enchey look down on the town.

It is the base for Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La, and for journeys on to North Sikkim and Pelling. Spring and summer are the main seasons. The monsoon (June–September) brings heavy rain and landslides that can cut the roads.

best_time.text: Spring and summer are the most popular seasons. Late April and May are mild, with highs rarely above 25 °C. Winter nights fall to about 5 °C, and Gangtok is often in fog in winter and the monsoon. The monsoon, June to September, brings torrential rain and landslides that can block the roads, so leave slack in your plans. Losar, the Tibetan new year, is celebrated with the Devil Dance in January–February.

local_transport.text: Taxis are the main public transport within Gangtok. Shared jeeps run longer routes around Sikkim. A 1 km cable car with three stops links lower Gangtok with the Legislative Assembly in the centre and is also a good way to see the town. MG Marg itself is best on foot.

items.title: Monsoon
items.body: June–September landslides can block roads to and from Gangtok. Build in buffer days and avoid travelling after heavy rain.

items.title: Fog
items.body: Mountain roads are often foggy in winter and the monsoon. Start drives early.

items.title: Can foreigners visit Nathu La?
items.body: No. Only Indian citizens may visit, Thursday to Sunday, with a permit obtained a day ahead in Gangtok.

items.title: Do I need a permit for Sikkim?
items.body: Many areas are restricted to foreigners and need official permits. Arrange them before heading out of Gangtok.

items.title: When is the best time to visit Gangtok?
items.body: Spring and summer. Avoid June–September if you can, since monsoon landslides often block the roads.

items.title: How do I get around Gangtok?
items.body: By taxi within town, shared jeep for longer trips, and the cable car for a scenic hop.
